The peach iced tea 🍑🫖 was refreshing but leaned towards being watered down, not very sweet, and had less ice than I would have liked.

The place has a cozy, welcoming vibe with good background music 🎵 that adds to the experience. The staff were warm, friendly, and attentive 🤗, which really made the visit pleasant.

For the peach iced tea, adding fresh mint leaves 🌿 would really lift the flavour, and it would be great if they asked customers whether they’d prefer more water or more ice. For the cheese chilli toast, offering an option of multigrain or brown bread 🍞 could be a nice touch for those who want to enjoy it without worrying too much about calories.

​Final Verdict
​Kafe 9 is a 5-star experience for anyone who appreciates good coffee and honest, tasty food. It’s clean, the atmosphere is great, and the open sitting makes it a breath of fresh air in the neighborhood.

I got to know that this food chain or Tea chain is in business since past almost 4 years and they currently have 4 outlets in Mumbai. Parking could be an issue for a 4-wheeler however you have space for 2-wheelers. So let's see what is good and bad.

Drinks/Beverages

This was a strong coffee mixed with bournvita or something similar. Chocolate powder was sprinkled over the top and on the rim of the glass. A straw is provided with it to slowly take it sip by sip. After getting impressed by the first item, we order some dishes (discussed later), we wanted something refreshing. I thought only mocktails were better with Guava but such soda drinks also go well.

Food

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Pibati is a charming little find for anyone who enjoys thoughtfully curated vegetarian food and well-made coffee. What instantly stands out is that the entire menu is 100% vegetarian, which is a big plus for people who specifically look for veg-friendly cafés without compromise on flavours or creativity.

We ordered quite a spread, starting with the Masala Avocado Toast, which was fresh, flavourful, and perfectly spiced without overpowering the natural taste of avocado. The Raw Papaya & Mango Bhel was a refreshing surprise — a lovely mix of crunch, tang, and sweetness that worked beautifully as a light starter. The Tadka Hummus had a desi twist and paired nicely with the accompaniments. For mains, the Aglio Olio Pasta was comforting, well cooked, and balanced in flavour. To finish, we enjoyed the Tiramisu Coffee and a Classic Cappuccino — both were satisfying and well brewed. We wanted to try their Matcha offerings, but we didn't order once they told us they still don't use Bree Matcha as their source of Matcha & we didn't want to risk having a bad Matcha experience.

Every dish we ordered tasted good, though the serving sizes could definitely be a little more generous, especially considering the pricing. One unique and interesting find was the Ghee Roast Croissant, which stood out for its creativity and flavour.

Seating-wise, the café has a small indoor area that accommodates around 15 people with roughly 6 compact tables, so it can feel a bit tight during peak hours. The outdoor seating is designated for smokers, so it’s best avoided if you’re visiting with kids. The service was prompt and courteous, which added to the overall positive experience.

Unfortunately, we were extremely hungry and only managed to click photos of the avocado toast before everything else arrived! Overall, Cafe Pibati is a great stop for vegetarian food lovers looking for quality food, good coffee, and a cozy café vibe — just with slightly limited seating and portion sizes. ✅☕🥑

I recently stepped into the Barista café located in Shimpoli, Borivali West, looking for a relaxing break. As always, the atmosphere was one of the highlights of the visit. The café maintained that classic, cozy Barista charm that makes it a reliable spot to unwind, catch up with friends, or simply enjoy some quiet time with a book. The ambient music and the general vibe were pleasant and inviting, setting a good stage for the food and coffee to follow.

The Coffee: The Usual Excellence
When it comes to the main event, the coffee, Barista did not disappoint. We decided to order two of their classic beverages: a Café Mocha and a Cappuccino.

· The Café Mocha was perfectly balanced. The rich, chocolatey flavor complemented the espresso without overpowering it, creating a smooth and indulgent treat. It was warm, comforting, and just the right amount of sweet.
· The Cappuccino was equally well-prepared. It had that perfect ratio of strong, robust espresso to velvety, micro-foamed milk. The foam was dense and creamy, making each sip a delight. Both coffees were spot on and met the high expectations one has for a dedicated coffee chain.

The Food: A Slight Misstep
However, the experience with the food was a bit of a mixed bag. We ordered the Cheese Garlic Bread to accompany our drinks. While the coffee shined, the garlic bread left something to be desired.

The concept is a classic café staple, but the execution felt lacking. The bread itself was adequately toasted, but the overall taste didn't quite hit the mark. I felt the garlic flavor could have been more pronounced and aromatic. More importantly, the "filling" aspect of the dish was underwhelming. The cheese was either too sparse or not distributed evenly, which meant that some bites were just dry bread without that essential gooey, cheesy pull you look for. For a dish that is meant to be a comforting, indulgent side, it ended up being a bit plain and forgettable.

The Verdict
In conclusion, Barista in Shimpoli remains a solid and reliable choice for coffee lovers. If you are in the area and craving a well-made Mocha or Cappuccino in a pleasant setting, this is definitely a spot to hit. However, if you are planning to build a meal around your coffee, you might want to manage your expectations regarding the food. There is certainly room for improvement on the snack side of things, specifically in making the garlic bread more flavorful and generous with the filling. It's a great place for a liquid pick-me-up, but the food needs a little more love to match the quality of the beverages.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters at IC Colony, and it was a thoroughly enjoyable experience. The coffee was among the best I have had—rich, well-balanced, and clearly prepared with care and attention to quality.

I also tried the Apple Crumble Cake, which paired exceptionally well with the coffee. The flavors complemented each other nicely and made the visit even more satisfying.

What stood out just as much as the food and beverages was the service. The staff were courteous, attentive, and genuinely focused on ensuring a pleasant customer experience. It was evident that they care about customer satisfaction, which added to the overall comfort of the visit.

I would certainly recommend this outlet to anyone looking for excellent coffee and a welcoming atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: Anugraha Ghale
featured_reviews.review_text:
impressed by how much presence this coffee brand has built across Mumbai. This particular IC Colony location maybe just how still the place was that afternoon. It wasn’t crowded, which already felt like a small gift in the middle of the city.

There are two floors. Upstairs for a slower pace, downstairs if you like watching the door open and close. We sat by the window upstairs, which I’d highly recommend; it has that simple magic of making ordinary moments feel a little cinematic.

Coffee had this faintly fermented undertone, interesting the more I sipped. We hadn’t asked what roast they used, and maybe that’s why it felt like tasting someone else’s mood for a change. Some might find that flavor unfamiliar, but I liked it.

The food came quickly. warm, comforting,. And that’s how the whole experience felt. just right. you can visit alone without feeling alone. The window will keep you company. The coffee will do the rest.

Staff doesn't force you to order anything (at least for the first hour) but you should still give their food a try because it's genuinely perfect.
